item.title: Professor Muhammad Yunus: A great leader in just one and a half years
item.description: After the student-people's uprising in August 2024, Bangladesh faced bloody chaos, economic ruin and deep instability in institutions. At that critical time, Nobel Prize winner Professor Muhammad Yunus took on the responsibility of leading the interim government. item.title: Milk-eggs-meat to be sold to 10 lakh families at subsidised prices in Ramadan
item.description: The government has taken an initiative to bring 10 lakh low-income families across the country under an affordable protein supply programme during the holy month of Ramadan.State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku said that protein-rich products will be sold at subsidised prices at 25 designated spots across the capital.He said this on Thursday morning at the inauguration of a programme to sell milk, eggs and meat at affordable prices at the conference room of the Livesto

item.title: Bill Gates cancels India summit speech to 'ensure focus' on AI
item.description: Bill Gates has cancelled his speech that was scheduled for Thursday at a major AI summit in India, the Gates Foundation said, after the Microsoft founder was named in the Epstein files."After careful consideration, and to ensure the focus remains on the AI Summit's key priorities, Mr. Gates will not be delivering his keynote address," the foundation said in a statement."The Gates Foundation remains fully committed to our work in India to advance our shared health and development goals," it said.

item.title: Sloppy Arsenal implode in 2-2 draw at bottom side Wolves
item.description: Teenager Tom Edozie scored a 94th-minute equaliser on debut as Arsenal let a two-goal lead slip at bottom side Wolverhampton Wanderers in a 2-2 draw on Wednesday, wasting a big chance to move clear in the Premier League title race.Arsenal have 58 points from 27 matches, five ahead of second-placed Manchester City having played a game more. item.title: Ramadan breaks to be used across English football again
item.description: The Premier League and English Football League will resume their procedures for Ramadan, with matches pausing briefly to allow Muslim players to break their fast, BBC reports.Ramadan starts this week and will last for a month. item.title: 3 service chiefs meet PM
item.description: The chiefs of the three services paid a courtesy call on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat on Thursday.Chief of Army Staff General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral M Nazmul Hassan and Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan met the Prime Minister at his office.Today is the second day for the Prime Minister at the Secretariat.Prime Minister's Adviser Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam was also present at the meeting.

item.title: Fakhrul launches website to receive info about extortion in Thakurgaon
item.description: Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has launched a website to receive information about extortion and other crimes in his home district of Thakurgaon.Fakhrul, lawmaker from Thakurgaon-1, urged residents of the constituency to directly inform him of any incidents of extortion, land grabbing, injustice, crime or other problems through the website.
